summary: Naomi Appleton works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. She earned her D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Christopher Minkowski and David Gellner. She was a British Academy Postdoctoral Fellow at Cardiff University and joined the University of Edinburgh.

Naoshiro Tsuji (1899–1979) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Oxford under Takakusu, Macdonell, Geldner, and Lévi. He served as Chair of Sanskrit at the University of Tokyo (1942–1960).

Naoya Funahashi (born 1937) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held posts at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science as a research fellow and at Otani University, attested in 1981.

Narada Maha Thera (1898–1983) was a Buddhist studies scholar educated at St. Benedict's College and University College, Colombo, and by Pelene Siri Vajirañāṇa. He served as Superior of Vajiraramaya Temple from circa 1955 to 1983.

Narayan Hemandas Samtani (born 1924) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at the University of Delhi, where he was also a research fellow, and served as Lecturer in Pali at Banaras Hindu University (~1963–1984).
Narendra Nath Bhattacharyya (1934–2001) worked in the fields of history, archaeology, religious studies, and Indology. He held an academic post at the University of Calcutta from circa 1967 to 1999.

Nariaki Nakazato (born 1946) is a historian and Indologist. He earned degrees at the University of Tokyo and a PhD from the University of Calcutta. He held posts at Kobe University and the University of Tokyo, where he was Professor (~1996–2010).
Narimoto Tamayama (1923–2002) was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at Taisho University, attested in 1974 and 1988.
Natalie Gummer works in Buddhist and religious studies. Attested at Harvard University in 2001, she became a professor of religious studies at Beloit College in 2001.

Natalie Maxwell (born 1942) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Wisconsin–Madison under Stephan Beyer, having also studied under Ngawang Wangyal, Khensur Ngawang Legden, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and Minoru Kiyota.
Natalie Rothman (born 1976) is a historian who studied at the University of Michigan (1999–2006). She joined the University of Toronto in 2006.

Natasha Heller specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from Harvard University in 2005, held a postdoctoral fellowship at UC Berkeley, and served as Assistant Professor at the University of California, Los Angeles.
Natasha Reichle works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her dissertation at the University of California, Berkeley, where she was supervised by Joanna Gottfried Williams.
Natasja Bosma (born 1981) is an Indologist who completed her PhD at the University of Groningen between circa 2012 and 2018 under the supervision of Hans T. Bakker.

Nathan Sivin (1931–2022) was a Sinologist and historian of science. Educated at MIT and Harvard (PhD 1966), he was a professor at MIT (1966–1977) and later Professor of Chinese Culture and History of Science at the University of Pennsylvania (1977–2006).

Nathan W. Hill (born 1979), a scholar of linguistics, Tibetology, and Sinology, studied at Harvard University. He was a reader at SOAS University of London (~2008–2019) and became the Sam Lam Professor in Chinese Studies at Trinity College Dublin in 2021.

Nathaniel Brassey Halhed (1751–1830) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Harrow School and Christ Church, Oxford. He served as an official for the East India Company from circa 1771 to 1785.

Nathaniel DeWitt Garson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under the supervision of Jeffrey Hopkins and also studied under Khenpo Namdrol.
Nathaniel Wallich (1786–1854) studied at the University of Copenhagen and served as Superintendent of the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden from circa 1817 to 1846.

Nathmal Tatia (born 1919) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He earned a Doctor of Literature at the University of Calcutta under Satkari Mookerjee and Sukhlal Sanghvi, and served as Director of the Jain Vishva Bharati Institute (attested 1982–1990).
